Now, I'm not saying that scripting should be added to subverses in the same way css is, because that would be a BAD bad idea, very easy to use maliciously. I think that there should be a way to have some sort of "script workshop", where users submit scripts that are then reviewed and approved, to minimise any sort of evil stuff that can be done. Every update is reviewed, too, to prevent any abuse. This way, things like expandos could be added as a script.

The other thing is this could also be used with CSS, so that themes like typogra or planate can be downloaded from a single source on the site, speeding up load times and saving bandwidth for both users and whoaverse.

Obviously this needs more thought before it can be implemented, because some simple oversight could cause huge issues down the road.
Some sort of way towards getting scripting

I think one of the reasons I'm reluctant about this kind of thing is how it'll be moderated. Scripts can be small and they can be big. If they are big, that's going to take some time to make sure that it's not malicious. How would 'malicious' be defined? It could take on a lenient or strict definition here, making a big difference in what code is accepted.

Who's going to moderate these scripts? Surely, scripts would be a big task, so a team would have to be devoted to it. It would have to be a team of both:

  • Trusted community members with free time on their hands.
  • Members adept in whatever scripting language to overlook the code.

Yeah, WhoaVerse isn't that big, so it's not really going to be that much of a problem to approve a script here or there, but what if WhoaVerse blows up? Would the feature have to be revoked or would it be approval only?

Don't get me wrong; I love scripts. They could make the experience here so much more awesome. I just think there's a whole lot to think about.

Yeah, I know. I think perhaps a size limit should be imposed so only small scripts are allowed, and malicious would be determined through 2 factors:

1) Does it do bad stuff such as steal credentials and send them to the author

2) Can the mods of a subverse use a script wrongly, such as by spamming popup windows

It is a lot to think about.
